name: manual_e73221
claim: An async function's 'I performed side-effect X, so set flag claimed=True to remember to clean it up on cancellation' pattern is NOT cancellation-safe if the flag is set on the line AFTER an awaited call that can itself be cancelled mid-flight after its underlying effect already happened. The cancellation-safe window is the gap between 'effect happened' (inside the awaited call, invisible to the caller) and 'caller's own flag reflects it' (the next line) -- a CancelledError landing in that exact gap causes the caller's cleanup handler to see claimed=False and skip releasing a resource that was actually already acquired.

decisions.notes: Confirmed real, Major-severity finding on oramasys/oramasys PR #1's GatewayLifecycle.run(): 'existing = await self._store.claim(key)' can have the store's implementation internally reserve the key before the await resumes; if cancelled in that window, the local 'claimed' bool never becomes True, so the except-CancelledError handler's 'if claimed: abort()' guard skips releasing the reservation -- the key leaks permanently and every later identical request blocks forever. The PR explicitly listed 'cancellation-safe claim release' as an already-solved safety property; it wasn't, for this exact acquisition window. General fix pattern: make the store's own claim() atomic with respect to cancellation (e.g. use asyncio.shield around only the reservation, or have claim() itself return a token whose absence unambiguously means nothing was reserved).
